item.text: You’ve fixed the stack and scope, so I’m taking the narrow-advice route: two concrete implementation steps centered on no-clobber renames, dry-run verification, and a disposable check before touching real photos.

1. Build a `plan_renames` path first, not a renamer first. Scan the target folder, read each photo’s timestamp from standard-library-available metadata only if present, otherwise fall back to filesystem modified time, then generate a deterministic target name such as `YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS[_NNN].jpg`; refuse any plan where two sources map to the same target or where a target already exists, and print a sorted preview table plus a summary instead of renaming anything. Acceptance behavior: running the tool on your 500-photo folder produces a complete rename plan with zero writes and explicitly marks every fallback timestamp and every conflict. Focused check: create a disposable test folder with 5-10 copied files including two same-second photos and one pre-existing destination filename; the command should show the exact planned names, add a suffix for same-second collisions, and abort on the pre-existing destination rather than overwriting it.

2. Add an `apply_plan` path that executes only a previously reviewed plan and uses fail-closed renames. Save the approved plan to a file, then require an explicit `--apply <plan-file>` mode that revalidates source existence and destination nonexistence immediately before each `os.replace` alternative choice; for no data loss, prefer `Path.rename()` / `os.rename()` semantics that fail if the destination exists on Windows rather than replacement-style behavior, and write a rename log as each file succeeds so an interrupted run is auditable. Acceptance behavior: after you review the dry run, applying the saved plan renames only the listed files, skips nothing silently, and stops on the first unexpected mismatch without clobbering any destination. Focused check: run `--apply` against the disposable test folder first, then simulate a stale plan by creating one destination file after preview; the tool should fail at that file and leave earlier successful renames recorded in the log.

If the dry run shows more than a few files falling back to filesystem timestamps instead of embedded photo dates, stop and inspect that sample before real use, because the naming rule may no longer match your actual intent.
